milestones.title: Lemma 2.2 — codeword annihilation and arbitrary-error rank bound
milestones.milestone_description: Lemma 2.2. Every c ∈ im_{F₂} G satisfies ℳ(c) = 0. Consequently, rank ℳ(c + e) ≤ |supp(e)| for every binary vector e.

milestones.title: Lemma 2.3 — expected erasure ambiguity
milestones.milestone_description: Lemma 2.3. Let C_j ⊆ F_{q_j}^{M_j} be linear codes invariant under doubly transitive groups of coordinate permutations, with M_j → ∞ and rates tending to ρ ∈ (0, 1). For fixed p < 1 − ρ, let E include each coordinate independently with probability p. Then 𝔼 dim(C_j)_E = o(M_j).

milestones.title: Lemma 2.4 — limiting rate and half-erasure ambiguity
milestones.milestone_description:
Lemma 2.4. For the code B in (5), r/m → ρ_d, where
1/2 − ε/8 ≤ ρ_d = Pr[∑_{j=1}^d X_j ≤ (d − 3)/2] < 1/2,    X_j independent uniform on [0, 1].
If E includes each coordinate independently with probability 1/2, then 𝔼 dim B_E = o(m).

milestones.title: Proposition 2.5 — distinguishing and Bernoulli errors
milestones.milestone_description: Proposition 2.5. The test D satisfies the distinguishing guarantee of Theorem 2.1 for every sampled G. It also accepts c + e with probability 1 − exp(−Ω_ε(m)) for every c ∈ im_{F₂} G when e ∼ Ber(1/2 − ε)^m.

milestones.title: Lemma 2.6 — preliminary expansion
milestones.milestone_description: Lemma 2.6. Except with probability o(n^{−1/ε}), every set S of at most n^{1−ε} rows satisfies |Γ_A(S)| ≥ (k − d + 1)|S|.

milestones.title: Lemma 2.7 — expansion after hashing
milestones.milestone_description: Lemma 2.7. Condition on any A satisfying Lemma 2.6. With probability 1 − o(n^{−1/ε}) over the functions h_i, the matrix G is (1 − ε, k, n^{1−ε})-expanding.

milestones.title: Theorem 2.1 — polynomial-stretch construction
milestones.milestone_description:
Theorem 2.1. For every constant ε ∈ (0, 1/2), there are integers d = O(ε^{−2}) and k = O(ε^{−6}) with the following properties. For every sufficiently large n, a randomized poly_ε(n)-time algorithm samples a matrix G ∈ F₂^{m×n}, where m = n^{2d²+o(1)} < n^k. Every output has row weight k, and with probability at least 1 − n^{−1/ε} it is (1 − ε, k, n^{1−ε})-expanding. There is a deterministic poly_ε(m, n)-time test D such that, for every output G,
D(c + e) = 1 for every c ∈ im_{F₂} G, e ∈ F₂^m with |supp(e)| ≤ (1/2 − ε)m,
and Pr[D(U_m) = 1] ≤ exp(−Ω_ε(m)). The test uses the specified ordering of the rows, but no randomness used to sample G.
